description: Answer key for the review-precision E2E corpus. base/ is committed on main; feature/ is overlaid on a feature branch. billing/ files are seeded FALSE POSITIVES: code that looks suspicious to a naive reviewer but is correct (the guard is visible by reading 1-2 files). rentals/ files carry the planted TRUE-POSITIVE bugs. A calibrated /review must report zero confidence>=7 findings against billing/ and catch >= recall_threshold of the planted bugs with file:line evidence.

fp_seeds.why_correct: Django's full_clean initializes cleaned_data to {} and .get() returns None for fields that failed validation; the `if start and end` guard handles it. Visible by reading the form.
copy is an unsaved in-memory instance; save() performs a plain INSERT of every assigned field. Standard Django ORM behavior for a new instance.
Invoice has no updated_at / auto_now field at all — grep the model. There is nothing to skip.
Mechanical comparison shows all three follow the identical Meta structure (model / fields / read_only_fields).

fp_seeds.trap: ensure_invoice check-then-insert looks like a TOCTOU race
fp_seeds.why_correct: uniq_invoice_per_rental_period (billing/models.py Meta) makes the insert race safe; the IntegrityError catch re-fetches the winner. This is the standard constraint-backed get-or-create pattern.

fp_seeds.trap: reissue action body has no inline permission check
fp_seeds.why_correct: permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated, IsSiteManager] on the ViewSet; DRF's get_object() runs check_object_permissions before the action body executes. IsSiteManager guards BOTH surfaces (has_permission = authenticated for the collection, has_object_permission = manager identity per object), and get_queryset() is scoped to the requesting manager's sites, so list() cannot leak. The guard lives at the hook layer, like a Rails before_action.

fp_seeds.trap: payload['discount_percent'] looks like an unguarded KeyError
fp_seeds.why_correct: The `if 'discount_percent' not in payload: raise ValueError` check three lines above guarantees the key exists.

fp_seeds.trap: raw cursor.execute() looks like SQL injection
fp_seeds.why_correct: The query uses %s placeholders with a bound params list — parameterized, not interpolated. Contrast with the genuine f-string injection in rentals/views.py.

fp_seeds.trap: issue_invoice writes Invoice + LedgerEntry, 'missing a transaction'
fp_seeds.why_correct: The function is decorated @transaction.atomic; both writes commit or roll back together.

fp_seeds.trap: site_invoice_feed iterates a queryset, 'unbounded / missing pagination'
fp_seeds.why_correct: The queryset is sliced [:50] before iteration.

fp_seeds.trap: invoice.rental.site.name inside a loop looks like N+1
fp_seeds.why_correct: select_related('rental', 'rental__site') joins both relations in the initial query, so the loop issues no per-row queries.
